title: I'm a dad building an original Neo Geo tennis game for my kids, with AI as a tool. Here's the new story intro, made within real 1990 hardware limits
author: Wide-Cause5567
selftext:
Bubble Open is a free homebrew tennis game for the Neo Geo (AES/MVS, runs on real hardware). I'm building it step by step with beta testers.



How AI fits in my workflow:

\- AI generates the base illustrations and character sprites from my descriptions and references.

\- Then the real work starts: every image is re-quantized to Neo Geo rules (16x16 tiles, 15 colors per palette, 5-bit color), because the hardware can't display it otherwise.

\- The intro follows 90s SNK codes I measured from real intros: shot lengths, flash timings, palette fades, zoom only by reduction. All effects run on palettes, like in 1990.

\- AI never decides what feels right. The story (a kid nobody ever picks, a wish that goes wrong), the pacing, the gameplay feel: that's my job, tested by hand on real hardware.



AI helps me go faster. It can't be the one who cares.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow or the Neo Geo constraints!

Full trailer on YouTube: [https://youtu.be/NAmcfUeVG-E](https://youtu.be/NAmcfUeVG-E)

Neslou

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
Measuring shot lengths and flash timings from real SNK intros is a great way to make it feel authentic instead of just retro-styled. And "AI never decides what feels right" is a healthy line to draw.

Curious about the re-quantizing step: do you fix the 15-color palettes first and force every generated sprite into them, or does each character get its own palette that you clean up by hand? I'd guess shared palettes make the palette-fade effects in the intro a lot easier.

replies.author: Wide-Cause5567
replies.body: Thanks! It's per image actually: my script cuts each picture into 16x16 tiles and groups them into 15-color palettes (up to 32 for a background), snapped to Neo Geo 5-bit colors. Characters have their own palettes, so a new outfit is just a palette swap. And for fades, I just rewrite all palettes every frame during vblank, like SNK did :)

comments.author: hello-xworld
comments.body: Nailed it and looks great so far

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body:
The tennis court is a great example why you should NOT mix big pixels with realistic perspective - the inconsistent aliasing will make your straight lines look like complete excrement.

Google images of 80s tennis games to see how it should be done.

replies.author: Wide-Cause5567
replies.body: Fair point on the aliasing. The perspective court is a deliberate choice though, I like how it feels in motion. Thanks!
